text:
cs_jordan: Heads up — Acme reporting a spike of 503/500s from hosted inference starting ~08:12 UTC. They provided request IDs and a few sample traces. Customer on a call in 5m. Initial look at gateway logs shows upstream worker exits (SIGSEGV / SIGBUS) and cuda memory allocation failures. Ticket INC-2026-141 created.

sre_bob: I'm pulling logs from the runner pods now. @oncall_liz can you take pager and start dmesg + nvml checks?

oncall_liz: Taking pager. Running: `kubectl logs -n hosted-runner runner-abc123 -c infer --tail=500` and `dmesg | tail -n 50` — seeing repeated OOM messages on GPU2/GPU3 and an `invalid device memory access` followed by `SIGBUS`. Sample from logs:
```
2026-03-17T08:13:02Z runner infer ERROR: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
2026-03-17T08:13:02Z runner infer FATAL: signal SIGBUS (code=1) at 0x7f8a2b3c
Backtrace (most recent call first): /opt/runtime/attn/kernel.cu:0x3fd
```

eng_runtime_ana: From a quick backtrace that looks like the kv-prefetch path hitting an unchecked allocation when context size is large. Noticed a model swap earlier at 02:00 UTC to `redwood-v2-large-ctx` — that increased memory by ~30% for long-context requests. Might be a regression in the prefetch/eviction logic.

mike_prodops: Temporary mitigation applied: routing Acme to fallback model `redwood-v2-small` and scaled dedicated pool by +2 instances. Added a per-customer soft rate limit (40 rps) while we triage. Route: `route:acme -> fallback_model:redwood-v2-small`

cs_jordan: Customer confirmed fewer 503s after routing but still sees intermittent timeouts for large-context requests. They also flagged duplicate charges for retries — can billing team look?

billing_bot: Automated alert: detected anomalous billing spikes for Acme (retries). Investigation opened: BI-334.

eng_runtime_ana: Repro steps I ran locally (minimal):
```
# stress harness (python)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME" -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-large-ctx","input":"<16k tokens payload>","batch_size":16}'
# this reliably causes a GPU mem spike and occasional SIGBUS in ~20% of runs
```

oncall_liz: Collected core dump and uploaded to S3: `s3://infra-dumps/INC-2026-141/core-runner-abc123.gz`. Host driver: nvidia-driver 525.85, CUDA runtime 11.8. Noted memory pressure rising before crash.

eng_runtime_ana: Core indicates segfault inside attention kernel memcpy path. My hypothesis: mismatch between compiled kernels and driver JITing when context+batch size cross a threshold -> out-of-bounds access. Also kv-prefetch is spiking resident GPU memory by ~18-25% on this model.

sre_bob: Proposed mitigation plan:
1) Keep Acme on fallback `redwood-v2-small` until stable.
2) Disable `kv_prefetch` for `large-ctx` model family via feature flag for 1h: `kv_prefetch=false`
3) Roll back the 02:00 model swap for hosted nodes that serve Acme.
4) Build hotfix with extra bounds checks + soft OOM handler in runtime; escalate patch to on-call eng for review.

eng_runtime_ana: I'll open PR for runtime guard rails and add an auto-backoff that drops prefetch when GPU memory > 90%. Also adding additional logging around allocation sizes.

cs_jordan: Customer wants ETA and compensation. Recommend offering credits for the impacted window — propose 50% credits for requests that received 5xx between 08:12-08:38 UTC. Please confirm.

mike_prodops: ETA for rollback + feature flag toggle: ~20 minutes. Hotfix build and QA will take longer; we should prioritize a quick rollback and global kv_prefetch toggle to stop the crashes.

deploy-bot: Rollout report: traffic migration executed — Acme routed to `redwood-v2-small` at 08:35 UTC (route id: r-789).

oncall_liz: Monitoring update: 5xx rate for Acme dropped from ~12% -> 1.6% after routing and disabling prefetch. Still seeing a couple of timeouts for very large requests; keeping an eye on tail latencies and GPU mem histograms.

cs_jordan: Removing customer from the call. I'll coordinate credits with finance and legal. Keep me posted on permanent fix timeline and a blameless postmortem.

eng_runtime_ana: Repro details for follow-up engineering: model swap + batch_size=32 + context=16k triggers the mem spike in ~80% of runs in the harness. Attaching minimal repro script in the incident doc.

oncall_liz: Filed incident doc and owners: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-141 (summary + artifacts + timelines). Owners: eng_runtime_ana (root cause), sre_bob (mitigation), mike_prodops (routing/billing coordination), cs_jordan (customer comms).

cs_jordan: Closing immediate escalation — mitigation in place, monitoring improving. Will keep this incident open for postmortem and follow-up action items (:white_check_mark:).
